column1: Kyou shukudai aru
column2: Do you have homework today? (informal)
column3: きょうしゅくだいある
column6: きょう|しゅくだい|ある
column8: Use the short form aru with rising intonation for an informal question. The particle ga can be omitted in casual speech.

column1: Uun shukudai nai
column2: No, I do not have homework. (informal)
column3: ううんしゅくだいない
column5: Do you have homework today? Answer in the negative.
column6: ううん|しゅくだい|ない
column7: no (informal)|homework|do not have / does not exist
column8: The short negative of aru is nai, not aranai.

column1: Nihonjin
column2: Are you Japanese? (informal)
column3: にほんじん
column6: にほんじん
column8: For an informal noun question, omit da and use rising intonation.

column1: Uun Nihonjin janai
column2: No, I am not Japanese. (informal)
column3: ううんにほんじんじゃない
column5: Are you Japanese? Answer in the negative.
column6: ううん|にほんじん|じゃない
column8: For nouns, use janai for the informal negative.

column1: Mainichi nihongo o hanasu
column2: Do you speak Japanese every day? (informal)
column3: まいにちにほんごをはなす
column6: まいにち|にほんご|を|はなす
column8: Hanasu is the dictionary / present short form of hanashimasu. Use rising intonation.

column1: Uun mainichi nihongo o hanasanai
column2: No, I do not speak Japanese every day. (informal)
column3: ううんまいにちにほんごをはなさない
column5: Do you speak Japanese every day? Answer in the negative.
column6: ううん|まいにち|にほんご|を|はなさない
column7: no (informal)|every day|Japanese language|object marker|do not speak
column8: Hanasu becomes hanasanai: change the final su to sa and add nai.

column1: Atsui
column2: Is it hot? (informal)
column3: あつい
column6: あつい
column8: An i-adjective can form an informal question by itself with rising intonation.

column1: Uun atsukunai
column2: No, it is not hot. (informal)
column3: ううんあつくない
column5: Is it hot? Answer in the negative.
column6: ううん|あつくない
column8: For an i-adjective negative, replace the final i with kunai: atsui → atsukunai.

column1: Yamashita sensei wa kakkoii to omoimasu
column2: I think Professor Yamashita is good-looking.
column3: やましたせんせいはかっこいいとおもいます
column6: やました|せんせい|は|かっこいい|と|おもいます
column8: Put a short-form clause before to omoimasu. Kakkoii is an i-adjective, so do not add da.

column1: Kono machi wa omoshirokunai to omoimasu
column2: I do not think this town is interesting.
column3: このまちはおもしろくないとおもいます
column6: この|まち|は|おもしろくない|と|おもいます
column8: Literally: I think this town is not interesting. Omoshiroi becomes omoshirokunai before to omoimasu.

column1: Mado o akenaide kudasai
column2: Please do not open the window.
column3: まどをあけないでください
column6: まど|を|あけないで|ください
column8: Akeru → akenai → akenaide kudasai. Use the short negative plus de kudasai for a negative request.

column1: Kasa o wasurenaide kudasai
column2: Please do not forget your umbrella.
column3: かさをわすれないでください
column6: かさ|を|わすれないで|ください
column8: Wasureru → wasurenai → wasurenaide kudasai: please do not forget.

column1: Tanaka-san wa daigakusei janai to iimashita
column2: Tanaka said that he is not a college student.
column3: たなかさんはだいがくせいじゃないといいました
column6: たなかさん|は|だいがくせい|じゃない|と|いいました
column7: Tanaka (polite name)|topic marker|college student|is not|quotation marker|said
column8: Use the noun negative janai before to iimashita (said).

column1: Tanaka-san wa kekkon shite inai to iimashita
column2: Tanaka said that he is not married.
column3: たなかさんはけっこんしていないといいました
column6: たなかさん|は|けっこん|して|いない|と|いいました
column7: Tanaka (polite name)|topic marker|marriage|do (te-form)|not in that state|quotation marker|said
column8: Kekkon shite iru means is married. Its short negative is kekkon shite inai.

column1: Mearii-san wa mainichi tanoshii to iimashita
column2: Mary said that every day is fun.
column3: メアリーさんはまいにちたのしいといいました
column6: メアリーさん|は|まいにち|たのしい|と|いいました
column8: Tanoshii is an i-adjective. Put it directly before to iimashita without da.

column1: Mearii-san wa amari sake o nomanai to iimashita
column2: Mary said that she does not drink sake much.
column3: メアリーさんはあまりさけをのまないといいました
column6: メアリーさん|は|あまり|さけ|を|のまない|と|いいました
column7: Mary (polite name)|topic marker|not much (with a negative)|sake|object marker|does not drink|quotation marker|said
column8: Amari pairs with a negative. Nomu becomes nomanai before to iimashita.

column1: Mearii-san wa mikan ga suki da to iimashita
column2: Mary said that she likes mandarin oranges.
column3: メアリーさんはみかんがすきだといいました
column6: メアリーさん|は|みかん|が|すき|だ|と|いいました
column7: Mary (polite name)|topic marker|mandarin oranges|marks what is liked|liked|plain copula|quotation marker|said
column8: The worksheet says likes. Suki is a na-adjective, so use suki da before to iimashita. Does not like would be suki janai to iimashita.

column1: Watashi wa e o kaku no ga jouzu desu
column2: I am good at drawing.
column3: わたしはえをかくのがじょうずです
column5: Which activity are you good at doing?
column6: わたし|は|え|を|かく|の|が|じょうず|です
column7: I|topic marker|picture|object marker|draw|turns the verb phrase into an activity|subject marker|skillful / good at|polite ending
column8: Use dictionary-form verb + no ga jouzu desu. E o kaku no means drawing pictures.

column1: Watashi wa supootsu o suru no ga jouzu janai desu
column2: I am not good at sports.
column3: わたしはスポーツをするのがじょうずじゃないです
column5: Which activity are you poor at doing?
column6: わたし|は|スポーツ|を|する|の|が|じょうず|じゃない|です
column7: I|topic marker|sports|object marker|do|turns the verb phrase into an activity|subject marker|skillful / good at|not|polite ending
column8: Supootsu o suru no means doing sports. Jouzu janai desu means am not good at. Heta desu is another way to say am poor at.

column1: Watashi wa jimu ni iku no ga suki desu
column2: I like going to the gym.
column3: わたしはジムにいくのがすきです
column5: Which activity do you like doing?
column6: わたし|は|ジム|に|いく|の|が|すき|です
column7: I|topic marker|gym|to (destination)|go|turns the verb phrase into an activity|marks what is liked|liked|polite ending
column8: Jimu ni iku no means going to the gym. Use dictionary-form iku, not ikimasu, before no ga.

column1: Watashi wa kuruma o unten suru no ga kirai desu
column2: I dislike driving a car.
column3: わたしはくるまをうんてんするのがきらいです
column5: Which activity do you dislike doing?
column6: わたし|は|くるま|を|うんてん|する|の|が|きらい|です
column7: I|topic marker|car|object marker|driving|do|turns the verb phrase into an activity|marks what is disliked|disliked|polite ending
column8: Kuruma o unten suru no means driving a car. Keep o after kuruma and no ga before kirai.
